tl;dr Book by Margret Cavendish in 1666 was probably read by Oda at some point and contains many references to a New World similar to One Piece.

The book is only a short poem, 2 chapters, and an epilogue. Short and very well written if you are interested in reading it for yourself.

How I stumbled on this: So lately I have been on this rabbit trail of Science Fiction. I have always had an affection for Lovecraft and Asimov, but lately I have been trying to branch into more Space Operas. This is all due to thread on recent interest in Kepler-452b. This thread drew my interest to Heinlein, Campbell, and Haldeman. But then I looking at /r/scifi today and this article about A Wrinkle in Time was linked. Notice the top comment talking about other women in SciFi literature.

Excerpt from comment:

Man, that surely had to be a flop that nobody heard of... what of "The Description of a New World, Called the Blazing-World" considered as one of the earliest works of SF, penned in 1666 by Margaret Cavendish, the Duchess of Newcastle?

New World and Cavendish—that can't be a coincidence...

Wikipedia describes Margret Cavendish as you would expect someone to describe Cabbage in One Piece:

In her memoir, Cavendish expresses that she enjoyed inventing herself through fashion. She states that she aimed for uniqueness in her dress, thoughts and behaviour, and remarks that she disliked wearing the same fashions as other women. She also expresses her desire to achieve fame. Several passages of her memoir remark upon her virtuous character, and she states that while she acknowledges the goodness in others, she thinks it acceptable that she should hope to be better than they are. Cavendish states that she hopes to have everlasting fame. Cavendish also notes that she expects to be criticised for her decision to write a memoir. She responds by stating that she wrote the memoir for herself, not for delight, but so that later generations will have a true account of her lineage and life.

and again here:

Cavendish states that she is not concerned that the best people like her writing, as long as a great many people do. She justifies this by linking fame to noise and noise to great numbers of people.

So then I looked at the Wiki for The Blazing World:

As its full title suggests, Blazing World is a fanciful depiction of a satirical, utopian kingdom in another world (with different stars in the sky) that can be reached via the North Pole. It is "the only known work of utopian fiction by a woman in the 17th century, as well as one of the earliest examples of what we now call 'science fiction' — although it is also a romance, an adventure story, and even autobiography."

A young woman enters this other world, becomes the empress of a society composed of various species of talking animals, and organizes an invasion back into her world complete with submarines towed by the "fish men" and the dropping of "fire stones" by the "bird men" to confound the enemies of her homeland, the Kingdom of Esfi.

So now having more interest I decided to see if the book was available on public domain (esp. since it was written in 1666). And it is: https://ebooks.adelaide.edu.au/c/cavendish/margaret/blazing_world/index.html

This Computer Attack Is Amazing, Frightening, and Unlike Anything Else. Its Called Rowhammer.

The fun stuff all happens on the 2nd page...if you're too lazy to click through, this is the awesome sauce.

Rowhammer takes advantage of a design defect in dynamic random-access memory, or DRAM, chips, which provide the high-speed data storage for a computer’s CPU. The most common DRAM standard today is called DDR3, ubiquitous on laptops, workstations, servers, phones, and tablets. A single DRAM chip contains billions of electrical capacitors, each of which stores a single bit. The sheer density of capacitors on these memory chips, however, causes a problem. By “hammering” a row of bits repeatedly, constantly changing their values, an attacker can sometimes induce an electrical interference in which capacitors in a different, adjacent row are mistakenly flipped. If the attacker can sufficiently control what’s in that adjacent row, then the attacker can manipulate your computer without authorization. Researchers at Google’s Project Zero were able to gain kernel privileges via Rowhammer and thus full read-write access to a computer’s memory.
That's fascinating - the boundary between hardware and software is always interesting.

I've found that sometimes eBay worked better for me at finding functional bike parts than established routes, such as Niagaracycle, and JensonUSA, Nashbar, etc., to name some of many.

So here's the cheapest handlebar tape and grips I've ever found:

http://www.ebay.com/itm/1-Pair-Bike-Racing-Bicycle-Motorcycle-Handle-Bar-Foam-Sponge-Grip-Cover-Nonslip-/261802382151?var=&hash=item3cf4a35347

These worked pretty well- if a bike's handlebars are too small, take an old inner tube and cut through it, and stuff it onto the handlebar. Then push these on over top. They're not the most amazing grips ever, obviously, but they do function well enough. Their principle downside is they absorb water like a sponge, so those morning commutes after a rain can get unpleasant. Still, they held up okay considering how amazingly cheap they were. Otherwise, I used a single, tore it in half, and used one half on each side. I would double it back and wrap the inside down with electrical tape at one end, then put an end cap on the other, like I was wrapping road handlebars.

http://www.ebay.com/itm/Road-Bike-Bicycle-Handlebar-Cork-Bar-Grip-Ribbon-Wrap-Tape-2Bars-Plug-2Adhesives-/201395879108?var=&hash=item2ee4213cc4

These in red have lasted on my Schwinn over two years now, though I admit to riding only every so often (about once a week or so on that bike), they're still in great, cushy condition. They've been through all kinds of weather and the like, though the bike is stored indoors/in a basement. I did finish off the wrap job with a spare stretch of black electrical tape I had lying around, because the finishing tape is always a bit sparse for my taste, and then I put the finishing tape they sent me over it- though in the last shipment, no finishing tape came along at all.

The material comes in a wide variety of colors and sizes, but there ARE bad ones out there that have thinner thickness, don't come with any finishing tape, etc., and sometimes use the same stock photos, so just a head's up. While what shipped was not terrible, it just did not have the same padded-out feel as some of the others. Maybe a manufacturing defect? Hard to tell. Also, if you're searching on your own, I recommend searching by price, ordering by lowest, then selecting 'buy it now,' unless you really like auctioning. Make sure it says you're getting a pair of them- once I ordered something then saw that it said "one roll." Whoops.
